native_language_semantic_policy: Native R scientific artist geometry implements source line/image/scatter coordinates, layout, common color limits, titles, labels and failure markers. case_evidence.description: Frozen Python public src/eyetrajectoriespy/sparse_multivariate_plotting.py::plot_sparse_mfpca_covariance_blocks. Joint 2-by-2 directional sparse planar covariance heatmap geometry with shared symmetric signed color limits

Real native paired direct sparse covariance/PACE scientific result and declared stage 'used' or 'smoothed'. Existing native source= keyword is backward compatible; frozen Python stage= alias is supported. Enforces no conflicting source/stage. Strict native mode does not accept Python Matplotlib axes objects.

Direct covariance Cxx,Cxy,Cyx,Cyy four fitted n-grid-square numerical arrays preserved exactly without swapping directional cross surfaces, with common vmax=max(abs(Cblocks)) and vmin=-vmax, default 1 if zero, imshow lower-origin grid extent, source per-axis labels and titles. Direct frozen Python public Matplotlib imshow get_array(), get_clim(), get_extent() source comparisons committed. Actual native rendering uses base R HCL Blue-Red 3 rather than bitwise Matplotlib coolwarm, and its shared source colorbar appears in metadata but not as identical Matplotlib rendered object.

Rejects non-native strict fit, invalid stage, incompatible source and stage, malformed covariance block dimensions and nonfinite covariance arrays. Python Matplotlib axes shape errors and exception identities remain native-specific.

Native strict source artist record exposes exact 2x2 layout, ordered source title text C_ab(s,t), common signed clim, source declared coolwarm cmap and colorbar label='covariance', source grid extent and four true covariance matrices. It is not a Python ndarray of Axes or a bitwise-identical Matplotlib Figure; native base R graphics backend remains different.

Directional paired joint PACE covariance operator: distinguish pre-PSD-smoothed blocks from the PSD-qualified operator actually used in eigenanalysis and score conditioning. No model selection or alternate covariance fitting.
